size.note: Newman's Birds gives 18–19 cm. Wikipedia gives 16–18 cm for the nominate race.

habitat: Relatively open broadleaved and Acacia woodland and mixed bushveld, usually perched high on an outer branch far from water. Not especially tied to rivers.
summary: A small grey-brown woodland kingfisher with a streaked crown, a bold black eye-stripe running round the nape above a white collar, and a two-coloured bill, dark above and red below. Blue shows mainly in flight or in the wing-opening display. The sexes are hard to separate: Wikipedia gives males a buffy-grey crown ground and a black underwing bar, and females a brownish crown ground without that bar. Newman's says the male's underwing is darker. No sexed photograph was verified.

similar.note: Brown-hooded is larger, with a heavier, wholly red bill, less obvious eye-stripes and buffy underparts (Newman's).
Woodland also has a bicoloured bill, but it is larger, with a bright turquoise back and white underparts (Newman's).

head.pattern: crown streaked dark brown on a buffy-grey ground (Wikipedia only)

wings.pattern: white linings, a black border, and a black bar at the base of the primaries (Wikipedia). Newman's says the male underwing is darker

head.pattern: crown streaked dark brown on a brownish ground (Wikipedia only)

wings.pattern: white linings and a black border, without the male's black primary bar (Wikipedia). Newman's says the female underwing is paler

bill.shape: dull red on the lower mandible (Wikipedia only)

viewNotes.note: Front-on, the off-white, streaked underparts and the two-tone bill (red below) stand out.
Side-on, the black eye-stripe running round the nape above the white collar is the best mark (Newman's).

Perched, the bird looks grey-brown above. The blue lower back, secondaries and tail are 'much more visible when the bird flies than when it is perched', or when it opens its wings in display (Wikipedia).
White wing-linings with a black border. Males also have a black bar at the base of the primaries, so the underwing looks darker; females lack that bar (Wikipedia; Newman's).
The blue lower back and secondaries show, with a white patch at the base of the primaries (Wikipedia). The display photograph shows this upperwing; it is not a flight shot.

calls.description: A 'tirrrrrr, deeeoo-deeeoo-deeeoo' (Newman's); a loud, ringing 'teeep-tiiii-rrrrrrr' and rollicking 'trrreerrr-treeerr' calls (eBird). Pairs duet while performing a wing-opening display, most often in the evening (Newman's). No source consulted assigns different parts to male and female.
